thread:
maya: quick note 1: compacted billing rows for partition p-12 lost original attribution after router remap. charge calc produced `unknown_tenant`.

liam: seen similar. root cause: router canonicalizes client_id then compactor drops the original field.

maya: lightweight fix idea: add an opaque `prov_envelope` at ingest (base64 blob, <=64b) that contains {version, origin_tenant, ingest_ts, key_id, sig}. treat as opaque unless compactor flag asks to preserve.

aprisa: pros: simple backfills (graft job can copy envelope into compacted rows), no global fingerprint table. cons: ~50B/event overhead.

cheng: alternative: stable fingerprint mapping table in the router. pros: smaller events. cons: big backfill when mappings change and messy late-arrival handling.

maya: rollout proposal: 1) write envelope at ingest (idempotent, add key_id) 2) add compactor flag `preserve_provenance: off|canary|on` 3) canary on 5% partitions for 48h 4) graft job to upsert missing envelopes for recent 14d window 5) switch audit indexing to prefer envelope.origin when present.

liam: monitoring: `envelope_absent_ratio`, `compactor_p95_ms`. alert if absent_ratio > 0.1% for 1h or p95 regresses >20% on canary.

aprisa: privacy: store envelope as opaque, redact on exports, only HMAC-verify in graft. add key rotation plan (monthly keys, graft accepts historical keys).

cheng: perf test needed: simulate compactor with preserve flag at production throughput and measure tail latencies.

deploybot: deploybot: scheduled canary (compactor v3) to prod-canary 5% partitions on 2026-03-24T02:00Z.

maya: I'll open the schema PR with envelope spec + compactor flag + graft runbook. tagging @cheng for perf tests.

liam: thanks. if canary looks good we flip and run reconciliation for last 30d. otherwise rollback and run best-effort offline graft.

maya: moving to action :thumbsup:
